name: separator
title: Separator
description: A one-pixel rule that divides groups of content.
docs:
## When to use - Between groups inside a menu, a card footer, or a settings list. - Between a toolbar and its content, horizontally or vertically. - Inside a stack of sections that would otherwise merge visually. ## When not to use - To create space. Use padding or `gap`; a rule is a boundary, not a spacer. - Between every list item. Repetition turns a boundary into noise — grouped spacing does the same job with less ink. - As a decorative flourish in a hero. Mark a purely visual rule as decorative so screen readers skip it: ```tsx ``` ## API | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | ------------- | ---------------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | | `orientation` | `"horizontal" \| "vertical"` | `"horizontal"` | Direction of the rule. | | `decorative` | `boolean` | `false` | Renders `role="none"` and `aria-hidden`; additive to upstream. | | `render` | Base UI render prop | – | Composition, as on every Base UI primitive. | | `className` | `string` | – | Merged last. | `data-slot="separator"` and `data-orientation` are always set, so a consumer can size the rule from CSS: `data-[orientation=vertical]:h-8`. ## Motion contract No motion (T0). A boundary that animates draws the eye to the wrong thing; if the layout changes, the surrounding `accordion` or `collapsible` owns that animation. | Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible | | ------- | ---------- | ----- | ------------- | | – | none | – | – | | reduced | none | – | – | | none | none | – | – | ## Accessibility - Base UI renders `role="separator"` with `aria-orientation`, which is the correct semantic for a group boundary. - `decorative` removes it from the accessibility tree for rules that carry no meaning (a divider inside a visual layout). - Focusable separators are not supported on purpose: a rule is not a control. ## Notes for AI - Prefer `gap` and `space-y` first; add a separator only when two groups need a visible boundary. - Never place a separator between two items of the same list. Group the list instead.
